title: Nested Learning: The Illusion of Deep Learning Architecture
authors: Ali Behrouz, Meisam Razaviyayn, Peilin Zhong, Vahab Mirrokni (Google; Zhong also Columbia). Correspondence: {alibehrouz, razaviyayn, mirrokni}@google.com. A version published at NeurIPS 2025.
date: arXiv v1: 31 December 2025 (2512.24695v1); NeurIPS 2025 version exists.
tldr: Nested Learning (NL) is a unifying paradigm that represents any machine-learning model TOGETHER WITH its training procedure as a single system of nested, multi-level, possibly parallel optimization problems, each an associative memory that compresses its own 'context flow' (tokens, gradients, or higher-level signals) at its own update frequency. Under this lens, backpropagation, momentum, Adam, AdaGrad, and Muon are all associative memories over gradients; attention is the non-parametric solution of a local L2 regression; linear attention / DeltaNet / Titans are parametric memories one level up from pre-training. The paper uses the framework generatively to build (1) more expressive optimizers (Delta Momentum, Deep Momentum GD, Delta Gradient Descent, Generalized GD, and the Multi-scale Momentum Muon M3), (2) a Continuum Memory System (CMS) — a chain of MLP blocks each updated at a different frequency, generalizing 'long-term vs short-term memory' — and (3) self-modifying Titans, where the key/value/learning-rate/gate projections are themselves test-time-updated memories that generate their own training targets. The combination, called Hope, outperforms Transformer++, RWKV-7, DeltaNet, Comba, TTT, Miras, DLA, and Titans at 760M/30B-token and 1.3B/100B-token scales, maintains BABILong accuracy out to 10M tokens, solves formal-language tasks (parity, a^n b^n c^n) with length generalization while remaining chunkwise-parallelizable, and enables continual learning (new-language translation, class-incremental classification) where plain ICL catastrophically forgets.
problem_and_motivation: LLMs are static after deployment: the only adaptive component is in-context learning, so knowledge lives either in the immediate context window (attention/KV) or in MLP weights frozen at 'end of pre-training'. The paper's analogy is anterograde amnesia — a patient who cannot consolidate new long-term memories and lives in the immediate present. Neurophysiology motivates two fixes the paper pursues: (i) online (synaptic) memory consolidation — the brain stabilizes fresh memories immediately, at multiple timescales set by brain-wave frequencies (fast gamma for sensory input, slow delta/theta for consolidation) — whereas deep nets use exactly two update frequencies, infinity (attention state, recomputed every token) and 0 (MLPs, frozen at test time); and (ii) the brain's uniform, reusable structure (memory distributed across regions, hemispherectomy patients recovering function) versus the apparent heterogeneity of modern stacks (attention + SSM + convolution + MLP). The paper argues this heterogeneity is an ILLUSION created by looking only at the solutions of optimization problems rather than the problems themselves: every component is a (linear or MLP) associative memory optimized with gradient descent, differing only in level, objective, and update frequency. Deeper stacking does not fix computational-depth limits (Merrill et al.), capacity scaling, optimizer suboptimality, or continual-learning failures; NL proposes a NEW axis — more nested LEVELS — as the way to get higher-order in-context learning and continual learning. Background scaffolding needed for inference-only readers: the whole paper presumes fluency with gradient descent, backpropagation (local error signals delta_l via chain rule), momentum/Adam/AdaGrad/Muon optimizers, and meta-learning (MAML-style bilevel optimization); each of these is defined in the paper's Section 2/4 and Appendix B and should be summarized for the target audience before presenting NL itself.
core_mechanism:
PART 0 — ASSOCIATIVE-MEMORY FOUNDATION. Definition 1 (from Miras): given keys $\mathcal{K}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{d_k}$ and values $\mathcal{V}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{d_v}$, an associative memory is an operator $\mathcal{M}(\cdot)$ found by $\mathcal{M}^*=\arg\min_{\mathcal{M}} 	ilde{L}(\mathcal{M}(K);V)$, where $	ilde{L}$ measures mapping quality. Terminology (from neuropsychology): 'memory' = a neural update caused by an input; 'learning' = acquiring effective memory. Keys/values need not be tokens — they can be gradients, sub-sequences, etc. One step of gradient descent on a loss $L$ has the proximal form $W_{t+1}=\arg\min_W \langle
abla_W L(W_t;x_t),Wangle+	frac{1}{2\eta_t}\|W-W_t\|_2^2$ (steepest descent in the Euclidean metric), and accumulated steps give the FTRL form $W_{t+1}=\arg\min_W\{\sum_{s=1}^t\langle
abla L(W_s;x_s),Wangle+	frac{1}{2\eta}\|W-W_1\|_2^2\}$ with solution $W_{t+1}=W_1-\eta\sum_s
abla L(W_s;x_s)$. These proximal/FTRL equivalences are the algebraic engine of every reinterpretation in the paper.

PART 1 — TRAINING IS AN ASSOCIATIVE MEMORY OVER SURPRISE. For a linear layer $y=Wx$, one SGD step factors as $W_{t+1}=W_t-\eta_{t+1}
abla_W L(W_t;x_{t+1}) = W_t-\eta_{t+1}\,
abla_{y_{t+1}}L(W_t;x_{t+1})\otimes x_{t+1}$, where $
abla_W L$ is the 'surprise' and $u_{t+1}:=
abla_{y_{t+1}}L$ is the Local Surprise Signal (LSS) in representation space (the local prediction error). Equivalently $W_{t+1}=\arg\min_W\langle Wx_{t+1},u_{t+1}angle+	frac{1}{2\eta_{t+1}}\|W-W_t\|_2^2$: training with backprop = an associative memory mapping each input to its local error. For a deep MLP with layers $\{W_\ell\cdot+b_\ell\}_{\ell=1}^L$, backprop computes $\partial L/\partial W_\ell=\delta_\ell\hat{x}_{\ell-1}^	op$ with $\delta_\ell=J_{\phi_\ell}(z_\ell)^	op W_{\ell+1}^	op\delta_{\ell+1}$ ($z_\ell$ pre-activation, $\hat{x}_\ell=\phi_\ell(z_\ell)$ layer output, $J$ the activation Jacobian), so layer $\ell$'s update $W_{\ell,t+1}=\arg\min_W\langle W\hat{x}_{\ell-1},\delta_\ellangle+	frac{1}{2\eta}\|W-W_{\ell,t}\|_F^2$ maps layer inputs to local error signals. CRUCIAL SUBTLETY: backprop is NOT linear attention on gradients, because the value $\delta_\ell$ is generated by the memory's own current state ($v_t=f_{W_t}(x_t)=-
abla_{y_t}L(W_t;x_t)$) — it is a SELF-REFERENTIAL memory (Schmidhuber 1993) that produces its own targets, which is exactly why it cannot be parallelized like a linear recurrence.

PART 2 — NESTED SYSTEMS AND LEVELS. Definition 2 (Update Frequency): any component $A$ (parametric like weights/momentum, or non-parametric like an attention block) has frequency $f_A$ = updates per unit time (one update on one data point = the time unit). Ordering $A\succ B$ if $f_A>f_B$, or $f_A=f_B$ but computing $B$'s state at time $t$ requires $A$'s state at $t$; incomparable components share a level (e.g., Adam's first and second moments — same frequency, independent computation). Components are sorted into ordered LEVELS: higher level = lower frequency. Definition 3 (Nested System): $K$ ordered levels, level $k$ holding optimization problems $\{(L_i^{(k)},\mathcal{C}_i^{(k)},\Theta_i^{(k)})\}_{i=1}^{N_k}$ (objective, context = the data stream it optimizes over, feasible parameter set), each solved by GD in proximal form $	heta_{i,t+1}^{(k)}=\arg\min_{\Phi}\langle\Phi x_{t+1},-
abla L_i^{(k)}(	heta_{i,t}^{(k)};x_{t+1})angle+	frac{1}{2\eta}\|\Phi-	heta_{i,t}^{(k)}\|_2^2$, $x_{t+1}\sim\mathcal{C}_i^{(k)}$; non-parametric solutions are also allowed for some 'boxes'. Definition 4 (NSAM, Nested System of Associative Memories): the same but every problem's context is key-value pairs $\mathcal{C}_i=\{(k_j^{(i)},v_j^{(i)})\}$; Appendix A gives the generalized forms (Definitions 6/7) replacing the linearized objective with the full $L_i^{(k)}(\Phi;x_{t+1})$ inside the proximal step. A 'neural learning module' = the joint representation of architecture + optimizer as one NSAM; the model's behavior is a property of the whole system (Transformer trained with SGD vs Adam is a DIFFERENT module). Worked examples: (a) 1-layer MLP + GD = 1-level memory mapping data to LSS; (b) GD+momentum = 2 levels — the inner level compresses gradients into the momentum memory, the outer applies the momentum state to the weights; (c) linear attention trained with GD = 2 levels — outer optimizes projections $W_k,W_v,W_q$, inner runs the recurrence $\mathcal{M}_t=\mathcal{M}_{t-1}+v_tk_t^	op$, itself one GD step on $	ilde{L}(\mathcal{M};k_t,v_t)=-\langle\mathcal{M}k_t,v_tangle$; (d) linear attention trained with momentum-GD = 3 levels. MLP vs 'Linear Attention++' (AdaTransformer): a Transformer block computes $y_{block}=y_{attn}W_{MLP}$ with $W_{MLP}$ frozen at level 1 (frequency 0); replacing the MLP with a linear-attention memory whose INITIAL state $\mathcal{M}_0=W_{LinAttn_{init}}$ is meta-learned in level 1 gives the identical algebraic form $y_{block}=y_{attn}W_{LinAttn}$ but with $W_{LinAttn}$ updated in-context at level 2 — i.e., recurrent memory modules ARE MLP blocks with one extra level; hybrids are Transformers whose MLPs gained in-context adaptation. Corollary on gating: when the initial memory state is NOT meta-learned (early linear Transformers, $\mathcal{M}_0=0$), the output gating by a linear layer plays the role of the missing persistent memory.

PART 3 — KNOWLEDGE TRANSFER BETWEEN LEVELS (the second design axis, alongside choosing the problems/frequencies). Five mechanisms between blocks $B^{(0)}$ (lower-frequency) and $B^{(1)}$ (higher-frequency): (1) Direct parametric conditioning $\mathcal{M}^{(0)}(\cdot):=\mathcal{M}^{(0)}(\cdot;\Theta^{(1)})$ or on the forward pass $\mathcal{M}^{(0)}(\cdot;\mathcal{M}^{(1)}(\cdot))$ — e.g., FWP fast weights feeding the slow net's output; no backprop crosses levels, each treats the other's state as a hyperparameter. (2) Direct non-parametric conditioning $\mathcal{M}^{(0)}(\cdot;\mathcal{C}^{(1)})$ — e.g., softmax attention conditioning on raw context. (3) Backpropagation across levels: shared gradient flow but different update frequencies, $\Theta^{(1)}_{t+1}=\Theta^{(1)}_t-\eta\delta_1\hat{x}_{t+1}^	op$, $\Theta^{(0)}_{t+1}=\Theta^{(0)}_t-\eta\delta_0 x_{t+1}^	op$ with $\delta^{(0)}$ obtained through the Jacobian chain — this is how CMS levels connect. (4) Initialization (MAML-style): $\Theta_0^{(1)}=\arg\min_\Phi\mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{C}\sim\mathcal{C}^{(0)}}[\ell(\mathcal{M}^{(1)}(\cdot;\Phi),\mathcal{C})]$ — meta-learning the inner memory's initial state (Titans/TTT do this; most linear RNNs do not). (5) Generation: one block generates the other's weights (hypernetworks) or its CONTEXT — the key example being that the ARCHITECTURE GENERATES THE OPTIMIZER'S CONTEXT (gradients), which holds for vanilla optimizers, not just learned ones, and motivates architecture-specific optimizers.

PART 4 — OPTIMIZERS AS MEMORIES AND NEW OPTIMIZERS. Momentum: $W_{\ell,t+1}=W_{\ell,t}+m_{\ell,t+1}$, $m_{\ell,t+1}=\alpha_{\ell,t+1}m_{\ell,t}-\eta_{\ell,t+1}\delta_\ell\hat{x}_{\ell-1}^	op$ solves (for $\alpha=1$) $\min_m\langle m\hat{x}_{\ell-1},\delta_\ellangle$ by GD ($\alpha
eq1$ adds L2 regularization on $m$): momentum is a value-less/Hebbian associative memory compressing past gradients, i.e., a low-pass filter. Capacity analysis: with decay $ eta=0.9$, the last 6 gradients carry >=50% and the last 43 carry >=99% of cumulative contribution — the optimizer forgets the gradient subspace of old tasks, causing catastrophic forgetting in continual learning with orthogonal task gradients (Eq. 45) — a failure of optimizer MEMORY MANAGEMENT, not model capacity. Adam (Appendix B): posit the element-wise objective $	ilde{L}_t=\sum_{i=1}^t\|m_{\ell,t}\odot g_{\ell,i+1}-P_{\ell,t}\|_2^2+\lambda_\ell\|m_{\ell,t}\|_F^2$ with $g=-
abla_W L$; the closed-form optimum is $m^*=(H+\lambda I)^{-1}\odot	ilde{M}\odot P$ where $	ilde{M}_{i+1}=	ilde{M}_i+ eta_1 g_{i+1}$ (first moment) and $H_{i+1}=H_i+ eta_2 g_{i+1}^2$ (second moment). Choosing $P_{\ell,t}=\sqrt{\sum_i g_i^2}$ (the gradient 'variance') yields $W_{i+1}\approx W_i-	frac{\eta}{\sqrt{ eta_2}}	ilde{M}_{i+1}/(H_i^{1/2}+\varepsilon)$ = Adam; so Adam is the OPTIMAL associative memory for the element-wise L2 objective mapping gradients to their variance. The outer-product version ($\|m g-P\|^2$, $H_{i+1}=H_i+ eta_2 g g^	op$) recovers AdaGrad-with-momentum; RMSProp/SignSGD/NAdam/AMSGrad/RAdam/Lion/Shampoo/SOAP follow by their known relations. Preconditioning: $W_{t+1}=W_t-\eta P_{t+1}^{-1}g_{t+1}$ where $P$ internally learns $\min_P	ilde{L}(P(\hat{g});g)$ — a nested memory mapping gradients to a chosen coordinate system. Muon: $W_{t+1}=W_t+\mathrm{NewtonSchulz}_k(m_{t+1})$; the orthogonalization objective $	ilde{L}(P(g);g)=\|P(g)^	op P(g)-I\|_F^2$ optimized by one GD step $O_{i+1}=O_i-\zeta(O_i-g_t+2O_i(O_i^	op O_i-I))$ (init $O_0=g_t$) recovers the degree-3 Newton–Schulz polynomial — so Muon's NS iterations are an INNER optimization level ($k$ internal steps per momentum update = more computation per neuron). abla L(W_i;x_i)-P_i)

abla L)$. (e) Nonlinear output: $W_{i+1}=W_i+\sigma(m_{i+1}(u_i))$; $\sigma=\mathrm{NewtonSchulz}$, linear $m$ recovers Muon. (f) Delta Gradient Descent (DGD): upgrade the LEARNING RULE ITSELF from dot-product to L2 regression: $W_{t+1}=\arg\min_W	frac12\|Wx_t-u_t\|_2^2+	frac{1}{2\eta_t}\|W-W_t\|_2^2$ with $u_t=-
abla_{y_t}L(W_t;x_t)$; for normalized inputs ($\|x_t\|_2=\lambda$), Sherman–Morrison (Appendix C: $(x_tx_t^	op+\eta_tI)^{-1}=	frac{1}{\eta_t}(I-	frac{1}{\lambda^2+\eta_t}x_tx_t^	op)$) gives the closed form $W_{t+1}=W_t(I-\eta_t'x_tx_t^	op)-\eta_t'
abla_{y_t}L(W_t;x_t)\otimes x_t$ with $\eta_t'=\eta_t/(1+\eta_t)$ — GD plus a data-dependent decay $(I-\eta'x x^	op)$ that accounts for correlation between samples (drops the i.i.d. assumption; the right rule for token space, where samples are highly dependent). (g) Generalized Gradient Descent (GGD, Definition 5): any self-referential memory $W_{t+1}=\arg\min_W	ilde{L}(x_t,u_t)+\mathrm{Ret}(W,\{W_i\}_{i=t-c+1}^t)$ with self-generated value $u_t=f_{W_t}(x_t)$; $\mathrm{Ret}$ keeps the solution near recent states. Analogously Generalized Momentum (GM).

PART 5 — ARCHITECTURES AS MEMORIES (Miras recap, all at the level above pre-training, with $k_t=x_tW_k$ etc. supplied by level-1 projections): softmax attention = NON-parametric solution of $\mathcal{M}^*=\arg\min_\mathcal{M}\sum_{i=1}^L s(k_i,q)\|v_i-\mathcal{M}\|_2^2=\sum_i rac{s(k_i,q)}{\sum_j s(k_j,q)}v_i$ (Nadaraya–Watson); restricting to the last $c$ tokens gives sliding-window attention. Hebbian RNNs (linear attention, RetNet, RWKV, lightning attention): GD+weight-decay on $	ilde{L}=-2\langle\mathcal{M}k_t,v_tangle$: $\mathcal{M}_t=\alpha_t\mathcal{M}_{t-1}+\eta_t v_t\phi(k_t)^	op$. Delta-rule RNNs (DeltaNet, Longhorn, RWKV-7): SGD on $	ilde{L}_t=\|\mathcal{M}_tk_t-v_t\|_2^2$ with retention $\|\mathcal{M}_t-\mathcal{M}_{t-1}\|_F^2$: $\mathcal{M}_t=(I-\eta_tk_tk_t^	op)\mathcal{M}_{t-1}+\eta_tv_tk_t^	op$. Oja (OjaNet): $\mathcal{M}_t=\alpha_t\mathcal{M}_{t-1}+\eta_t(v_t\phi(k_t)^	op-\mathcal{M}_{t-1}^	op v_t)$ = GD on $	ilde{L}=-2\langle\mathcal{M}k_t,v_tangle+\|\mathcal{M}^	op v_t\|_2^2$. Omega rule (Atlas): non-online window update $\mathcal{M}_t=\alpha_t\mathcal{M}_{t-1}-\sum_{i=t-c+1}^t\gamma_{t,i}	ilde{L}(\mathcal{M}_t;\phi(k_i),v_i)$ over a cached window of $c$ inputs; $L_p$-norm attentional biases (Miras) generalize the L2 objective.

PART 6 — CONTINUUM MEMORY SYSTEM (CMS). A chain of MLP blocks $\mathrm{MLP}^{(f_1)},\dots,\mathrm{MLP}^{(f_k)}$, each with chunk size $C^{(\ell)}:=\max_i f_i\cdot C/f_\ell$ (i.e., level $\ell$ updates every $C^{(\ell)}$ tokens). Forward: $y_t=\mathrm{MLP}^{(f_k)}(\mathrm{MLP}^{(f_{k-1})}(\cdots\mathrm{MLP}^{(f_1)}(x_t)))$. Update (Eq. 71): $	heta^{(f_\ell)}_{i+1}=	heta^{(f_\ell)}_i-\eta^{(\ell)}\sum_{t=i-C^{(\ell)}}^{i}f(	heta_t^{(f_\ell)};x_t)$ if $i\equiv0\ (\mathrm{mod}\ C^{(\ell)})$, else no update — where $f(\cdot)$ is the error term of an arbitrary optimizer (e.g., $
abla L$ for GD) and $L$ is the TASK objective (next-token prediction), so each block compresses its own recent context into weights; the standard Transformer MLP is the degenerate $k=1$, frequency-0 case. Three wiring variants: (i) Nested CMS — level $s$ meta-learns the initial state of level $s{+}1$ ($	heta_0^{(f_{s+1})}=\arg\min_\Phi\mathbb{E}_{T\sim\mathcal{C}^{(s)}}[\ell(\Theta,T;\Phi)]$), and each block is re-initialized to its meta-learned init when its context window ends (higher-order ICL); (ii) Sequential CMS — blocks in series, ALL initial states meta-learned by backprop at the lowest-frequency level; (iii) Independent (head-wise) CMS — parallel blocks with different context lengths, combined by $y_t=\mathrm{Agg}(\mathrm{MLP}^{(f_k)}(x_t),\dots,\mathrm{MLP}^{(f_1)}(x_t))$, e.g., a learnable weighted sum. Why it helps continual learning: knowledge forgotten from a fast block $\mathrm{MLP}^{(f_s)}$ usually survives in slower blocks $s'<s$, and backprop-based knowledge transfer of initial states can CYCLE it back — a loop in the time dimension that makes hard forgetting unlikely. WHY each design choice: multi-frequency = brain-wave analogy + amortized cost; per-level chunked accumulation = restores sequence parallelism inside chunks; meta-learned inits = fast adaptation and stability (knowledge transfer from pre-training level). Ad-hoc level stacking (Sec 7.3): initialize CMS blocks from a pre-trained Transformer's MLPs, $\mathrm{MLP}_0^{(f_i)}=\mathrm{MLP}_{pretrained_i}$; the inner learning rate $\eta^{(\ell)}$ interpolates between frozen pre-trained behavior ($\eta	o0$) and full adaptation — this is how Llama-3 models are retrofitted for the continual-learning experiments.

PART 7 — SELF-MODIFYING (SELF-REFERENTIAL) TITANS. Motivation: Transformer projections $W_k,W_v,W_q$ are frozen in-context, bounding how tokens can be contextualized (a 1-layer Transformer's projection sees only the token + position); short convolutions/canon layers only mix locally. Fix: promote every projection to a test-time-updated memory. Step 1 (fully adaptive memory): $k_t=\mathcal{M}_{k,t-1}(x_t)$, $v_t=\mathcal{M}_{v,t-1}(x_t)$, $q_t=\mathcal{M}_{q,t-1}(x_t)$, $\eta_t=\mathcal{M}_{\eta,t-1}(x_t)$ (inner learning rate), $\alpha_t=\mathcal{M}_{\alpha,t-1}(x_t)$ (retention/forget gate); each $\mathcal{M}_\square$ and the main $\mathcal{M}_{mem}$ optimize $\min L(\mathcal{M}_\square;k_t,v_t)$ with some optimizer; output $y_t=\mathcal{M}_{mem,t}(q_t)$; ALL initial states $\mathcal{M}_{\square,0}$ meta-learned across sequences (essential for fast adaptation, stability, noise robustness). Step 2 (self-modification): instead of sharing $v_t$ as everyone's target, each memory GENERATES ITS OWN VALUE $\hat{v}_{\square,t}=\mathcal{M}_{\square,t-1}(v_t)$, i.e., the model produces its own training targets and thereby learns its own update algorithm (Schmidhuber's self-referential weight matrix lineage); $q_t=x_tW_q$ is kept as the only non-adaptive projection. Step 3 (learning rule): because tokens are correlated, use DGD with weight decay as the inner optimizer: $\mathcal{M}_{\square,t}=\mathcal{M}_{\square,t-1}(\alpha_tI-\eta_tk_tk_t^	op)-\eta_t
abla L_{\mathcal{M}_{\square,t-1}}(\mathcal{M}_{\square,t-1};k_t,\hat{v}_{\square,t})$ for $\square\in\{k,v,q,\eta,\alpha,\mathrm{memory}\}$, with objective $L(\mathcal{M};k,v)=\|\mathcal{M}(k)-v\|_2^2$. Memory architecture: 2-layer residual MLP $\mathcal{M}_\square(\cdot)=(\cdot)+W_{\square,1}\sigma(W_{\square,2}(\cdot))$ (arbitrary in principle, need not match across components). Linear-memory special cases: dot-product objective gives $\mathcal{M}_{\square,t}=\mathcal{M}_{\square,t-1}(\alpha_tI-\eta_tk_tk_t^	op)-\eta_t\hat{v}_{\square,t}k_t^	op$; L2 objective gives $\mathcal{M}_{\square,t}=\mathcal{M}_{\square,t-1}(\alpha_tI-\eta_tk_tk_t^	op)-\eta_t(\mathcal{M}_{\square,C\lceil t/Cceil}k_t-\hat{v}_{\square,t})k_t^	op$.

PART 8 — HOPE. Hope block = self-modifying Titans (small state, expressive DGD rule) feeding a CMS chain (large capacity, simple rule) — deliberately complementary. Forward (Eqs. 94–97, normalization/conv omitted): $o_t=\mathcal{M}_{mem,t-1}(q_t)$ with all self-modifying updates as above, then $y_t=\mathrm{MLP}^{(f_k)}(\cdots\mathrm{MLP}^{(f_1)}(o_t))$. Practical details: $q,k$ are L2-normalized; local convolution of window 4. Hope-Attention variant: replace the self-modifying Titans with softmax global attention (isolates the CMS contribution). M3 OPTIMIZER (CMS applied to optimization; Algorithm 1): maintain fast momentum $M_t^{(1)}=M_{t-1}^{(1)}+ eta_1g_t$ every step, slow momentum $M_t^{(2)}=M_{t-1}^{(2)}+ eta_3\sum_{i=(k-1)f}^{kf}g_i$ updated once per $f$ steps (chunk $\hat{C}$), Adam-style second moment $V_t=V_{t-1}+ eta_2g_t^2$; orthogonalize both momenta $O^{(j)}=\mathrm{NewtonSchulz}_T(M^{(j)})$ and update $\Theta_t=\Theta_{t-1}-\eta(O_t^{(1)}+\alpha O_t^{(2)})/(\sqrt{V_t}+\epsilon)$ — 'Adam + Muon + CMS', the independent-CMS aggregation being the weighted sum. It is a proof of concept for CMS in the gradient context flow (long-memory momentum akin to AdEMAMix but via delayed updates rather than tuned decay).
outer_loop_training: What is meta-learned at pre-training time: (1) for Hope, the INITIAL STATES $\mathcal{M}_{\square,0}$ of all six self-modifying memories ($\square\in\{k,v,q,\eta,\alpha,mem\}$, each a 2-layer residual MLP) plus the one static projection $W_q$, embeddings, convolutions, norms, and the initial parameters of every CMS MLP level; (2) for CMS specifically, the per-level initializations are trained through backprop at the lowest-frequency level (Sequential variant) or level-by-level (Nested variant, where level $s$ meta-learns level $s{+}1$'s init and the block re-initializes at context end). This is knowledge-transfer-via-initialization (MAML-form, Eq. 72/73): the outer objective is expected task loss (next-token prediction) over contexts, so gradients flow THROUGH the inner-loop updates — the outer gradient of the NTP loss backpropagates through the unrolled DGD recurrence of each memory and through the chunked CMS updates. The paper frames pre-training itself as level-1 in-context learning whose context flow IS the pre-training corpus, optimized by AdamW (which is itself, per Appendix B, a two-level nested memory: first/second moments at one frequency, weights below). Chunkwise parallelization (Sec 8.2), which makes outer-loop training feasible: split the length-$L$ sequence into $\lceil L/C\rceil$ chunks; freeze each memory at its state from the END of the previous chunk, $\mathcal{M}_{\square,C\lceil t/C\rceil}$, when (a) generating all keys/values/self-targets/learning-rates/gates for the whole next chunk and (b) taking the inner gradient $\nabla L(\mathcal{M}_{\square,C\lceil t/C\rceil};k_t,\hat{v}_{\square,t})$ — so all inner gradients for a chunk are computable in parallel before the chunk is processed, admitting the fast dual/parallel form of TTT (Sun et al. 2024) and Titans (Behrouz et al. 2025c). Two different chunk sizes are used in practice: one for $\mathcal{M}_{mem}$ and one shared by all other memories. This chunking is EXACTLY what breaks the self-referential seriality: within a chunk the value-generator is a stale snapshot, which is the approximation that buys parallel training. CMS training parallelism: for tokens with $i\not\equiv0\ (\mathrm{mod}\ C^{(\ell)})$ there is no sequential dependence inside the chunk, so all such positions process in parallel; only the boundary updates are sequential. Note the contrast the paper itself draws: true backprop cannot be parallelized this way because its values are state-dependent (self-referential); the chunkwise scheme is the engineered compromise. Scaffolding flag for inference-only readers: 'gradients flowing through the inner loop' means the pre-training autograd graph contains the entire per-token/per-chunk weight-update recurrence of the fast memories — conceptually identical to backpropagating through an optimizer, which is what makes these models expensive to TRAIN but is invisible at serving time.
inner_loop_test_time: What changes during inference, per token (Hope): six memory modules — $\mathcal{M}_k,\mathcal{M}_v,\mathcal{M}_q,\mathcal{M}_\eta,\mathcal{M}_\alpha,\mathcal{M}_{mem}$, each a 2-layer residual MLP $(\cdot)+W_1\sigma(W_2(\cdot))$ — update their weights via the DGD-with-weight-decay rule $\mathcal{M}_{\square,t}=\mathcal{M}_{\square,t-1}(\alpha_tI-\eta_tk_tk_t^\top)-\eta_t\nabla L(\mathcal{M}_{\square,t-1};k_t,\hat{v}_{\square,t})$, where the learning rate $\eta_t$ and retention gate $\alpha_t$ are THEMSELVES produced by adaptive memories (input-dependent optimizer hyperparameters), and each memory's regression target $\hat{v}_{\square,t}=\mathcal{M}_{\square,t-1}(v_t)$ is self-generated. In deployment the same chunkwise schedule as training is used (updates every $C_\square$ tokens with generation from the previous chunk's snapshot), so per-token amortized cost = (forward passes through 6 small MLPs) + (1/C x per-chunk parallel inner-gradient computation, itself a few matmuls per memory per token) + the CMS forward. Additionally the CMS MLP chain updates level $\ell$ once every $C^{(\ell)}$ tokens by accumulating the task-loss error signal over the chunk (Eq. 71) — i.e., at inference the model keeps running truncated gradient steps of the NTP objective on its own context, at geometrically spaced frequencies; the paper quotes an average update cost of order $O(\tfrac{1}{\hat{f}}\cdot\tfrac{L_{layer}}{5}\cdot d_{in}^2)$ parameters touched per step for a 4-level CMS with top frequency $\hat{f}$ (small relative to a full forward). State size: unlike a KV cache growing $O(L)$, Hope's inference state is CONSTANT in sequence length but large per layer — the full parameter tensors of 6 two-layer MLPs plus the drifted CMS weights (state IS weights). No optimizer beyond the built-in rule is needed at test time for the fast memories (the DGD rule and gates ARE the optimizer; the ablation's 'w/o Momentum' row implies the deployed inner rule also carries a Titans-style momentum term); CMS levels use 'the error component of an arbitrary optimizer' — in experiments plain accumulated gradients. Ablations (Table 6, ppl/acc): full Hope 12.24/58.1; replace DGD with plain GD 13.41/56.5; remove momentum 13.58/56.9; remove weight decay 13.71/57.2; remove CMS 13.04/57.3; freeze inner k 13.77/56.9; freeze inner v 13.90/55.1; freeze inner q 12.19/57.4 (slightly BETTER ppl — consistent with the final design keeping q static). Continual-learning corollary: because 'end of pre-training' discards optimizer state, momentum memories (knowledge about the loss landscape) are lost; in NL terms a continually-learning module should retain those lower-frequency levels too.

concepts_introduced.name: Nested Learning (NL)
concepts_introduced.definition: Paradigm representing a model plus its optimization as an interconnected system of nested/multi-level/parallel optimization problems, each with its own context flow, objective, and update frequency; architectures and optimizers are the same concept at different levels.

concepts_introduced.name: Context flow
concepts_introduced.definition: The data stream a given optimization problem/level compresses — tokens for sequence blocks, gradients for optimizers, sub-sequences or higher-level signals for other levels.

concepts_introduced.name: Neural Learning Module
concepts_introduced.definition: The joint representation of architecture + training/optimization process as one system; the unit of design in NL (a Transformer+SGD and a Transformer+Adam are different modules).

concepts_introduced.name: Nested System / NSAM (Nested System of Associative Memories)
concepts_introduced.definition: K ordered levels of optimization problems (L_i^(k), C_i^(k), Theta_i^(k)) each solved by (proximal) gradient descent; NSAM is the special case where every problem is an associative memory over key-value pairs (Definitions 3/4; generalized Definitions 6/7 in Appendix A).

concepts_introduced.name: Update frequency & levels (Definition 2)
concepts_introduced.definition: f_A = number of updates per unit time for component A; components ordered by frequency (ties broken by computational dependence) into levels — higher level = lower frequency; attention has f=infinity, frozen MLPs f=0.

concepts_introduced.name: Local Surprise Signal (LSS)
concepts_introduced.definition: The output-space gradient u_t = nabla_y L(W_t;x_t) — the local prediction-error signal a layer memorizes against its input under the backprop-as-associative-memory view.

concepts_introduced.name: Backprop as self-referential associative memory
concepts_introduced.definition: Training maps inputs to self-generated values v_t = -nabla_y L(W_t;x_t); because values depend on the memory's own state, backprop is NOT linear attention over gradients and is inherently sequential.

concepts_introduced.name: Delta Gradient Descent (DGD)
concepts_introduced.definition: Learning rule from L2-regression proximal objective; closed form (normalized inputs, Sherman–Morrison): W_{t+1} = W_t(I - eta' x_t x_t^T) - eta' nabla_y L (outer) x_t — GD with input-dependent decay capturing sample correlations.

concepts_introduced.name: Generalized Gradient Descent (GGD) / Generalized Momentum (GM)
concepts_introduced.definition: Any self-referential memory W_{t+1} = argmin ~L(x_t,u_t) + Ret(W, recent states) with self-generated value u_t = f_{W_t}(x_t); family containing GD, DGD, etc.

concepts_introduced.name: Delta Momentum
concepts_introduced.definition: Momentum whose internal objective is L2 regression on gradients instead of dot product, yielding a delta-rule update with gradient-dependent decay and better memory management of past gradients.

concepts_introduced.name: Deep Momentum Gradient Descent (DMGD)
concepts_introduced.definition: Momentum parameterized as an MLP (not a matrix), updated by GD on its own internal objective; increases the optimizer-memory's capacity for past gradients.

concepts_introduced.name: Muon-as-nested-optimization view
concepts_introduced.definition: Newton–Schulz orthogonalization = one-step-GD solutions of ||P(g)^T P(g) - I||_F^2, i.e., an inner level learning a mapping of momentum to an orthogonal coordinate system (k inner steps per outer update).

concepts_introduced.name: Adam as optimal associative memory
concepts_introduced.definition: Appendix B: Adam is the closed-form optimum of an element-wise L2 objective mapping gradients to their running variance; AdaGrad is the outer-product analogue; first/second moments are two same-level parallel memories.

concepts_introduced.name: Continuum Memory System (CMS)
concepts_introduced.definition: Chain (or parallel bank) of MLP blocks, level ell updated every C^(ell) tokens with accumulated task-loss error; generalizes long/short-term memory to a frequency spectrum; Transformer MLP = k=1, frequency-0 special case. Variants: Nested, Sequential, Independent/head-wise (Agg-combined).

concepts_introduced.name: Multi-scale Momentum Muon (M3)
concepts_introduced.definition: Optimizer = Adam second moment + two Newton–Schulz-orthogonalized momenta at different frequencies (fast per-step + slow per-chunk), aggregated by weighted sum; CMS applied to the gradient context flow.

concepts_introduced.name: Self-modifying (self-referential deep) Titans
concepts_introduced.definition: Sequence block where k, v, eta (learning rate), alpha (retention gate), and the memory itself are 2-layer-MLP memories updated in-context by DGD, each generating its own regression target hat-v = M(v_t); q stays static; all initial states meta-learned.

concepts_introduced.name: Hope / Hope-Attention
concepts_introduced.definition: Hope = self-modifying Titans + CMS chain in one block (the paper's flagship continual-learning architecture); Hope-Attention swaps the Titans part for softmax attention to isolate CMS.

concepts_introduced.name: AdaTransformer / Linear Attention++
concepts_introduced.definition: Didactic construction: Transformer whose MLP is replaced by linear attention with meta-learned initial state — algebraically an MLP with an added in-context level; grounds the claim 'recurrent models are MLP blocks with one more level'.

concepts_introduced.name: Parametric vs non-parametric in-context learning
concepts_introduced.definition: All levels do ICL on their own context flow; Transformers do non-parametric ICL (closed-form Nadaraya–Watson solution over raw context), recurrent/TTT models do parametric ICL (compress context into weights); 'test-time training/memorization' = parametric ICL; pre-training = ICL with the corpus as context; ICL is not emergent but structural (a consequence of having >=2 levels).

concepts_introduced.name: Knowledge-transfer taxonomy
concepts_introduced.definition: Five inter-level mechanisms: direct parametric conditioning, direct non-parametric conditioning, cross-level backprop, initialization (MAML), and generation (hypernetworks; architecture generating gradients as the optimizer's context).

concepts_introduced.name: Ad-hoc level stacking
concepts_introduced.definition: Initializing CMS levels from a pre-trained model's MLP weights; inner learning rate interpolates between frozen pre-trained behavior and full in-context adaptation — the retrofit recipe used for Llama-3.

concepts_introduced.name: Continual Translation of a Novel Language (CTNL)
concepts_introduced.definition: New benchmark combining MTOB (Kalamang) and Manchu: learn two unseen languages sequentially in-context, then translate both to English; measures in-context catastrophic forgetting.

concepts_introduced.name: Omega rule (imported from Atlas)
concepts_introduced.definition: Window-based (non-online) memory update over the last c cached inputs, M_t = alpha_t M_{t-1} - sum gamma_{t,i} ~L(M_t; phi(k_i), v_i); collapses to the online case for uniform weights and full window.

assumptions_and_scope: NL's definitions restrict inner optimization to (proximal) gradient descent — the paper argues this is not limiting since everything from attention (non-parametric solutions are explicitly allowed for some boxes) to Adam fits, but rules like full Newton or non-GD solvers sit outside Definitions 3/4 (Appendix A generalizes slightly). The DGD closed form requires normalized inputs (||x_t||=lambda, satisfied by normalization layers) for the Sherman–Morrison step. The equivalences are mostly at the level of ONE gradient step per token with specific objectives (dot product or L2) — e.g., 'Adam is the optimal associative memory' is with respect to one particular posited objective (Eq. 101) and a particular choice of target P (gradient variance); the reverse-engineering is suggestive, not unique. Frequency ordering treats attention as frequency infinity and frozen weights as 0, a modeling convention. The self-referential claims are softened in practice: exact self-reference is sequential, and the trained/served system uses chunkwise stale snapshots, so the deployed model is an approximation of the mathematical object. Chunk sizes, number of CMS levels, and frequencies are hyperparameters chosen empirically (2K lowest-frequency flagged as a good efficiency/quality tradeoff). Scale is capped at 1.3B params / 100B tokens for from-scratch training and Llama-3-8B for retrofits; no wall-clock throughput or memory numbers are reported for Hope itself (only for the M3 optimizer); the Cartridges comparison is explicitly deferred due to incomparable compute profiles. The neuroscience is motivation, not mechanism (only ONLINE consolidation is addressed; offline/sleep replay is explicitly out of scope). Catastrophic forgetting is explicitly NOT claimed solved — forgetting is framed as a necessary consequence of finite-capacity compression. The 'w/o inner-projection q' ablation slightly improving perplexity indicates not every added level pays off, i.e., level placement matters and is currently empirical.
experiments_and_scale: (1) Language modeling + common-sense reasoning, from scratch on FineWeb-Edu + long-context mix, 32K vocab, AdamW: 760M params / 30B tokens and 1.3B / 100B tokens. Baselines: Transformer++, Samba (hybrid), RetNet, DeltaNet, RWKV-7, Comba, TTT, Miras(Memora), DLA, Titans. Hope headline: 760M — Wiki ppl 18.68, LAMBADA ppl 20.07, avg acc 52.28 (best; Titans 51.68, RWKV-7 50.55); 1.3B — Wiki ppl 14.39, LAMBADA ppl 10.08, avg 58.04 (Titans 56.82, Samba 54.46, Transformer++ 53.38); gains grow with scale. (2) RULER NIAH (trained ~50B tokens): Hope best attention-free across S-NIAH-1/2/3 and MQ/MK/MV at 4K–16K (e.g., S-NIAH-3 16K: Hope 24.8 vs Titans 21.2, RWKV-7 5.8; MK-NIAH 16K: Hope 14.8 vs Titans 8.2); Hope-Attention beats Transformer on S-NIAH-1 (100 vs 76–89). (3) BABILong: Hope (fine-tuned, small) stays competitive to 10M tokens where Titans and ARMT degrade after ~1M and GPT-4-class models fail by 128K–256K; RAG-Llama-8B plateaus lower. (4) Continual learning: class-incremental CLINC (150 intents)/Banking (77)/DBpedia (70) with Llama3-8B/3B retrofitted via ad-hoc level stacking + 15B-token continual pre-training — Hope beats ICL, EWC, and InCA (external-learner SOTA). CTNL (MTOB Kalamang + Manchu, ChRF): sequential two-language setup collapses ICL, while Hope-1/2/3 improve monotonically with levels; Hope-3 nearly recovers single-language performance. Level ablations on MK-NIAH/LongHealth/QASPER: more levels help; lowest-frequency 512 best, 2K near-parity and much cheaper. (5) Short in-context recall (SWDE/NQ/DROP/FDA/SQuAD/TQA): Transformers still best (e.g., FDA 67.3 vs Hope 41.9), Hope best attention-free (beats Titans/RWKV-7/Comba everywhere). MAD synthetic: Hope best overall incl. beating Transformers (compression 51.2, fuzzy ICR 52.1, memory 85.2). (6) Formal-language recognition (Irie et al. 2023 construction): parity, (aa)*, (abab)*, a^n b^n, a^n b^n c^n, Shuffle-2 — Hope 100.0 on all incl. the out-of-distribution length bin (Bin1), matching LSTM/SRWM while (unlike them) keeping parallelizable training; Transformer and linear attention/DeltaNet fail most Bin1 cases. (7) Optimizers: M3 vs AdamW vs Muon on ViT-24M/86M, ImageNet-21K (11M images, 10,450 classes, patch 16) — best train and test loss; efficiency on 140M/1.3B Transformer LM training: M3 slower than Muon (multiple momenta + extra NS), on par with AdaMuon. (8) Hope component ablation (Table 6): every component except the inner q-projection contributes (numbers in inner_loop_test_time field).
systems_implications: STATE VS KV-CACHE MATH: Hope replaces an O(L*d) growing KV cache with O(1)-in-L but weight-sized state: per Hope block, 6 two-layer residual MLP memories (each 2 weight matrices, so state ~12 matrices of roughly d x d_hidden per block) plus the CMS chain whose MLP weights themselves drift at inference. Serving state is therefore per-sequence MUTABLE WEIGHTS — the single most disruptive property for inference infra: no weight sharing across concurrent requests for the fast levels, checkpoint/restore of a conversation means persisting these tensors, and batched serving needs per-request copies of all six memories (same class of problem as Titans/TTT/Atlas serving, but with ~6x more fast-weight tensors than a single-memory Titans block, partially offset by chunked update frequency). CMS adds slowly-mutating MLPs: the paper's amortized estimate is O((1/f-hat) * (L_layer/5) * d_in^2) parameters touched per step for a 4-level CMS with top frequency f-hat, and levels with C^(ell)=2K update only every 2K tokens — the paper explicitly identifies 'lowest frequency = 2K' as the efficiency sweet spot because update frequency directly sets forward-pass cost. PARALLELIZATION: training and prefill use the chunkwise-dual scheme of TTT/Titans — freeze memory snapshots at chunk boundaries, generate the whole chunk's k/v/self-targets/eta/alpha in one batched pass, compute all inner gradients w.r.t. the frozen snapshot in parallel, apply the accumulated update at the boundary; within a CMS chunk there is NO sequential dependence at non-boundary positions. Two distinct chunk sizes (main memory vs auxiliary memories) are a kernel-design degree of freedom. The DGD linear-case update M(alpha_t I - eta_t k_t k_t^T) - eta_t(...)k_t^T is a generalized delta rule, so DeltaNet-style WY/UT-transform chunk kernels are the natural template for linear-memory variants; the deployed memories are MLPs, so kernels are batched small-GEMM sequences like TTT-MLP rather than a single scan. DECODE: token-by-token generation pays 6 extra small-MLP forwards + amortized update matmuls per block; arithmetic intensity is GEMM-dominated (accelerator-friendly), latency flat in context length — the usual linear-model win over attention at long L, with crossover at short L (Transformers still win short recall, Table 3). SELF-REFERENCE VS PARALLELISM: the paper is explicit that true self-referential updates (values generated from the CURRENT state, as in exact backprop) forbid linear-recurrence-style parallelization; the stale-snapshot chunking is the engineered compromise, and chunk size is a fidelity/throughput dial. OPTIMIZER SIDE: M3 needs 2 momentum buffers + 1 second-moment buffer + 2 Newton–Schulz pipelines per matrix — measured slower than Muon, on par with AdaMuon at 140M/1.3B (Figure 12), with acknowledged scaling concerns; the slow momentum's chunked accumulation is bandwidth-friendly (one fused accumulation per f steps). RETROFIT PATH: ad-hoc level stacking converts an existing pre-trained Transformer (MLPs -> CMS levels initialized from pre-trained MLP weights + 15B-token continual pre-training) — a practically important deployment story: continual-learning capability without from-scratch pre-training. CONTINUAL SERVING: NL erases the train/serve boundary — in the intended deployment the model is ALWAYS applying truncated NTP gradient updates to CMS levels on user data, which raises infra questions the paper does not address (per-tenant weight divergence, rollback, provenance/safety of self-updated weights).
connections: WITHIN THE SIX-PAPER SET: this is the capstone/theory paper of the Behrouz et al. Google line and explicitly cites the earlier entries: Titans (2501.00663, Behrouz et al. 2025c) supplies the deep-memory-with-momentum-and-forget sequence block, the meta-learned initial memory state, and the chunkwise training procedure Hope inherits; Miras / 'It's All Connected' (2504.13173, Behrouz et al. 2025b) supplies Definition 1 itself (associative memory + attentional-bias objective + retention + inner optimizer as the design space) and the L_p-norm objectives referenced in Section 5 — NL is essentially Miras extended from 'a sequence block is one optimization problem' to 'the ENTIRE model + optimizer is a nested system of them'; Atlas (2505.23735, Behrouz et al. 2025a) supplies the Omega rule (windowed, non-online updates) and the DLA baseline used throughout the experiments. Hope is best read as: Titans with (i) all projections and gates promoted to self-modifying fast memories (SRWM lineage), (ii) the inner rule upgraded from GD to DGD (state-dependent decay = delta rule at the OPTIMIZER level), and (iii) the frozen MLP replaced by CMS. The other papers in the study set (2511.07343, and 2606.03979 which postdates this one) should be cross-checked for whether they adopt NL vocabulary (levels, CMS, self-modification) — NL supplies the unifying terminology the set converges on. EXTERNAL LINEAGE: fast weight programmers (Hinton & Plaut 1987; Schmidhuber 1992; Ba et al. 2016; Schlag et al. 2021) give the two-level slow/fast reading NL generalizes to K levels; Schmidhuber's self-referential weight matrix (1993) and SRWM (Irie et al. 2022b) are the direct ancestors of self-modifying Titans (SRWM appears as a formal-language baseline — matching accuracy but without parallelizable training, Hope's stated edge); linear attention (Katharopoulos et al. 2020) = Hebbian rule; DeltaNet (Schlag et al. 2021), Longhorn (Liu et al. 2024b), RWKV-7 (Peng et al. 2025) = delta rule; gated/retention variants (RetNet, Gated-DeltaNet-style decay) are subsumed as retention-gate choices in Eq. 65's family; OjaNet (Irie et al. 2022a) = Oja's rule; TTT-Linear/TTT-MLP (Sun et al. 2024) supply the test-time-training frame, the Nadaraya–Watson attention view, and the chunkwise dual form — NL reframes TTT as 'parametric in-context learning' and objects to the 'test-time' name in continual settings; Mamba/SSMs enter via Samba (hybrid baseline) and the state-tracking literature (Merrill et al. 'The Illusion of State in State-Space Models' — this paper's title is a deliberate echo); Muon (Jordan et al. 2024) is both reinterpreted (Newton–Schulz = inner optimization) and extended (M3); AdEMAMix (Pagliardini et al. 2025) and Multiscale Muon (Selvaraj & Pappone 2025) are acknowledged parallel multi-momentum approaches (controlled decay vs M3's delayed updates); MAML (Finn et al. 2017), hypernetworks, and learned optimizers are all classified as knowledge-transfer special cases; Cartridges (Eyuboglu et al. 2025) is the acknowledged alternative for long-context knowledge incorporation (comparison deferred); mesa-optimization (von Oswald et al. 2023) connects to the Omega-rule window collapse; Wang et al. 2025 test-time regression is the closest independent unifying framework. WHAT IT LEAVES OPEN relative to lineage: architecture-specific optimizers are named but not delivered; offline consolidation (replay/sleep) deferred; level/frequency schedules hand-designed, not learned.
open_questions: (1) Catastrophic forgetting is explicitly NOT solved — the paper frames forgetting as inherent to finite-capacity compression, and CMS only shapes WHERE and HOW FAST it happens; principled capacity allocation across levels is open. (2) Level design is empirical: how many levels, what frequencies, which components deserve their own level (the inner-q ablation shows added levels can hurt), and whether frequencies/schedules can be learned rather than fixed. (3) Serving economics are unquantified: no throughput/latency/memory measurements for Hope; per-request mutable-weight state, batching, and multi-tenant isolation for a model that continually gradient-updates itself in production are unaddressed. (4) M3 has acknowledged computational overhead and unproven scaling to large networks; the promised co-design of architecture-specific optimizers ('design optimizers for the gradient distributions a given architecture generates') is left entirely to future work. (5) The chunkwise stale-snapshot approximation to true self-reference lacks a fidelity/chunk-size analysis; exact self-referential updates remain sequential — is there a better parallelization? (6) Fine-tuning is required for the 10M-token BABILong results; zero-shot compression at that scale fails for all small models — how to get long-context capacity without task-specific adaptation. (7) Comparison with Cartridges-style self-study approaches deferred. (8) Offline consolidation (the second, sleep-replay stage of biological memory) is explicitly out of scope — a natural sequel is a background 'replay' level. (9) Theory: the associative-memory reverse-engineerings (e.g., Adam's objective) are existence arguments, not uniqueness results; no formal expressivity theorem for K-level NSAMs (e.g., how computational depth grows with levels) is proven — the claim rests on state-tracking experiments. (10) Scale: 1.3B/100B is the ceiling for from-scratch runs; whether Hope's edge over tuned Transformer++ persists at 7B+ is untested.
